title: Operate on recorded engineering work through reliable explicit commands
statement: Engineers and engineering agents need a reliable command-line interface for inspecting recorded work, recording explicitly chosen engineering decisions, and recovering interrupted updates without losing information or mistaking mechanical command success for engineering authority.

what.problem: Published command behavior, record preservation, and failure outcomes are not explicit in the initial REM model; broad knowledge and change capabilities alone do not explain how callers safely operate on the delivered recording interface. Callers should not have to navigate operational storage files or manage manifests to obtain context or record decisions; separate local history also needs explicit availability and recovery outcomes.
what.desired_outcome: Callers obtain a coherent current handoff and record explicit decision-relevant changes through supported tasks, without managing storage layout or reconstructing activity history.

why.rationale: Automation and people depend on predictable commands, precise selection, preserved neighboring work, and outcomes that separate storage success from approval. The same responsibility applies when multiple local agents share operational records and when storage realization changes.

stakeholders: Engineers and reviewers operating on recorded engineering work
Engineering agents acting on explicit actor decisions
Maintainers and consumers of the published command-line interface

conditions: When selecting a command, inspecting project facts or exact recorded work, preparing or saving a decision, retrying or recovering an interrupted operation, and investigating an invocation.
When several local agents inspect or update the same project work, when history is absent or unavailable, and when explicitly creating, restoring, transferring or migrating operational backups.

contexts: The published local command-line interface, selected project operational records and retained evidence artifacts, explicit engineering subjects, backup/restore destinations, and private diagnostics; initially one checkout and one user with one or more local agents.

how.approach: Provide bounded current-state reads and explicit updates with actor attribution, reference integrity, stale-write protection, atomic publication and truthful recovery outcomes. Retain selected history only under its declared scope; unavailable information is not empty state or approval. IR-003 owns handoff and retention meaning; this IR owns reliable commands.

how_much.scope: Covers command admission, discovery, selected reads, explicit recording, concurrent local access, transaction recovery, result projection and private diagnostics, extended to supported operational backup, restoration, transfer and migration commands. SR-040–047 and new SR-078 express the revised draft operational obligations. Current allocations and source-observed facets describe the successor v2/v4 scope. SR-078 cross-Change history query remains a separate draft capability, excluded from this adoption. Earlier assessments retain their exact original subjects and do not establish coverage of new obligations. Installation content and policy remain separately owned. The scope does not introduce command support for editing REM design JSON, a workflow decision engine, hosted services, distributed history merging or new platform/performance guarantees. Database transaction recovery and backup restoration remain distinct operations; a fresh engineering checkout alone supplies no operational-history availability claim.

assumptions: The selected local execution environment and destination storage support the requested operation; unavailable sources or destinations require explicit outcomes.
Operational restoration relies on the usable-backup scope and retention assumptions owned by IR-003. No hosted backup or recovery of destroyed copies is implied.
constraints: The CLI does not grant permission, choose workflow progression, or infer actor decisions from role labels, record shape, or command success.

The detailed contracts under MOD-010 Command handling and MOD-011 Work record storage retain authority for command behavior and independent version domains; relocation does not adopt or reinterpret a historical protocol.
